title: South Carolina Public Universities: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility, 4 Measured | SignalFeed.dev
description: How South Carolina public universities stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 13% of 186 sampled PDFs untagged, 2% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: South Carolina: Title II PDF backlog at public universities
body:
South Carolina has 5 public 4-year universities with 5,000+ students in the federal IPEDS directory. Public universities are covered by the ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H), and most are part of state government, which puts them on the April 26, 2027 compliance date. Web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to South Carolina?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers South Carolina's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions and dates. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these institutions link from their main websites. This page summarizes South Carolina as a whole. It does not name or rank individual institutions. See the national university page for the method.

South Carolina at a glance

  • 4 of 5 institutions measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). Of the rest, 0 blocked our crawler and 1 had too few PDFs on their main site to sample (some host documents on other systems). That is not a clean result.
  • 186 PDFs analyzed. 13.4% had no accessibility tags, lower than the national figure of 26.7%. 2.1% were scanned images with no usable text, 18.8% did not declare a document language, and 42% had no document title.
  • Spread: at none of the 4 measured institutions more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; at 2, fewer than 1 in 10 were. The most common main issue was no document title (2 of 4 institutions).
  • 0 of 12 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured institution has roughly 178 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured institutions that is on the order of 5,600 pages.
  • 48% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for a South Carolina university

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA and are common in catalogs, policies, forms and board materials. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section. Our ADA Title II PDF guide walks through it.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.

Per-institution data

The South Carolina workbook lists every targeted public university in the state, with PDFs found and estimated, untagged and scanned shares, recent-document share, estimated pages failing basic checks and days to the compliance date. It is built for remediation firms, consultants and agencies planning work.

Per-institution rows for South Carolina are available on request: email us.
